subproblem.title: Monotone compact exhaustion modulo a null set (σ-compact metric space)
subproblem.statement: Let X be a σ-compact metric space with its Borel σ-algebra, μ any measure on X, and A ⊆ X μ-null-measurable with μ(A) < ∞. Then there are compact sets Q_0 ⊆ Q_1 ⊆ Q_2 ⊆ … contained in A with μ(A ∖ ⋃_j Q_j) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MetricSpace X] [SigmaCompactSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (μ : Measure X) (A : Set X), NullMeasurableSet A μ → μ A < ⊤ → ∃ Q : ℕ → Set X, (∀ j, IsCompact (Q j)) ∧ (∀ j, Q j ⊆ A) ∧ Monotone Q ∧ μ (A \ ⋃ j, Q j) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof Part II, Step 3 (item 13): 'Exactly as in Theorem 1.8 (finite Borel measure 𝓗^{m+k} restricted to a Borel A₀ ⊆ A with 𝓗^{m+k}(A∖A₀) = 0 is inner regular by compact sets on the σ-compact metric space X) there are compact Q_1 ⊆ Q_2 ⊆ ... ⊆ A (take finite unions) with 𝓗^{m+k}(N) = 0, N := A∖∪_j Q_j.' This is the compact-approximation step of Simon's printed proof of Theorem 1.8(i): 'the regularity property 1.15(2) of Ch. 1 together with the σ-compactness of X implies that we can take a sequence K_1, K_2, ... of compact sets in X with K_j ⊆ A for each j and Hᵐ(A ∖ (∪_j K_j)) = 0', stated here for an arbitrary measure μ and with the K_j replaced by their monotone finite unions; the parent applies it with μ = 𝓗^{m+k}.

Proof.
1. (Borel kernel.) Since A is μ-null-measurable, there is a Borel set B ⊆ A with B = A μ-almost everywhere (`NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq`); in particular μ(A ∖ B) = 0 (`ae_le_set`).
2. (Finite restriction.) Let ν := μ.restrict B, i.e. ν(S) = μ(S ∩ B) for every S ⊆ X (`Measure.restrict_apply'`, B measurable). Then ν(X) = μ(B) ≤ μ(A) < ∞, so ν is a finite Borel measure on X.
3. (Compact inner regularity of ν.) Claim: for every Borel S ⊆ X and every ε > 0 there is a compact K ⊆ S with ν(S ∖ K) < ε. (a) Closed regularity: let 𝒮 be the class of Borel sets S such that for every ε > 0 there are a closed F and an open U with F ⊆ S ⊆ U and ν(U ∖ F) < ε. Every closed set C belongs to 𝒮: take F := C and U_n := {x : dist(x, C) < 1/(n+1)} (for C = ∅ take U = ∅); the open sets U_n decrease to C, so ν(U_n ∖ C) → 0 by continuity from above of the finite measure ν. 𝒮 is closed under complements (if F ⊆ S ⊆ U then Uᶜ ⊆ Sᶜ ⊆ Fᶜ with Uᶜ closed, Fᶜ open and Fᶜ ∖ Uᶜ = U ∖ F) and under countable unions: for S = ⋃_j S_j with S_j ∈ 𝒮 and ε > 0 choose closed F_j and open U_j with F_j ⊆ S_j ⊆ U_j and ν(U_j ∖ F_j) < ε·2^{-(j+2)}; put U := ⋃_j U_j (open) and, using continuity from below of ν on the increasing sets ⋃_{j≤J} F_j, choose J with ν(⋃_j F_j ∖ ⋃_{j≤J} F_j) < ε/2 and put F := ⋃_{j≤J} F_j (closed, a finite union). Then F ⊆ S ⊆ U and, since U ∖ ⋃_j F_j ⊆ ⋃_j (U_j ∖ F_j), ν(U ∖ F) ≤ ν(U ∖ ⋃_j F_j) + ν(⋃_j F_j ∖ F) ≤ Σ_j ε·2^{-(j+2)} + ε/2 = ε/4 + ε/2 < ε. Hence 𝒮 contains all Borel sets. (b) Compactness: since X is σ-compact there are compact L_0 ⊆ L_1 ⊆ ... with ⋃_n L_n = X (`compactCovering`, `iUnion_compactCovering`, `isCompact_compactCovering`, `compactCovering_subset`). Given Borel S and ε > 0, take a closed F ⊆ S with ν(S ∖ F) < ε/2 by (a); the compact sets F ∩ L_n increase to F, so by continuity from below ν(F ∖ L_n) < ε/2 for some n, and K := F ∩ L_n ⊆ S is compact with ν(S ∖ K) < ε. [In Mathlib this is available directly: for the finite measure ν on the σ-compact metric space X the instance `Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure` gives `Regular ν`, hence `InnerRegularCompactLTTop ν`, and `MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_sdiff_lt` gives the compact set.]
4. (Choice of compacts.) For every j ∈ ℕ choose by step 3 a compact K_j ⊆ B with ν(B ∖ K_j) < 1/(j+1). Put Q_j := K_0 ∪ K_1 ∪ ... ∪ K_j (`Set.accumulate K j`). Each Q_j is compact as a finite union of compact sets (`isCompact_accumulate`), Q_j ⊆ B ⊆ A, and Q_j ⊆ Q_{j+1}, i.e. j ↦ Q_j is monotone (`monotone_accumulate`).
5. (Null remainder.) Let P := ⋃_j Q_j. Since B is Borel and B ∖ P ⊆ B, μ(B ∖ P) = μ((B ∖ P) ∩ B) = ν(B ∖ P). For every j, K_j ⊆ Q_j ⊆ P, so B ∖ P ⊆ B ∖ K_j and ν(B ∖ P) ≤ ν(B ∖ K_j) < 1/(j+1). Letting j → ∞ (`ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero`, `ge_of_tendsto'`) gives μ(B ∖ P) = 0. Finally A ∖ P ⊆ (A ∖ B) ∪ (B ∖ P), so μ(A ∖ P) ≤ μ(A ∖ B) + μ(B ∖ P) = 0 + 0 = 0 (`measure_union_le`). Thus (Q_j) is a monotone sequence of compact subsets of A with μ(A ∖ ⋃_j Q_j) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Replace A by a Borel B ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ B) = 0.
ν = μ restricted to B is a finite Borel measure on the σ-compact metric space X, hence inner regular by compact sets.
Choose compact K_j ⊆ B with ν(B ∖ K_j) < 1/(j+1) and take the monotone finite unions Q_j = K_0 ∪ … ∪ K_j.
μ(B ∖ ⋃Q_j) = ν(B ∖ ⋃Q_j) ≤ 1/(j+1) for all j, so μ(A ∖ ⋃Q_j) ≤ μ(A ∖ B) + μ(B ∖ ⋃Q_j) = 0.

audit.reason: The measurable kernel, finite restricted measure, compact approximation and accumulated finite unions prove the exact contract; the supplied Lean witness also checks. Step 3 explicitly supplies a valid direct Regular/exists_isCompact_sdiff_lt argument. Its redundant expanded derivation has a nonblocking arithmetic typo: Σ_{j≥0} ε·2^{−(j+2)} equals ε/2, not ε/4. The supplied direct library argument independently closes that step, so no additional proof obligation is needed.

subproblem.title: Borel measurability of y ↦ 𝓗^k(Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}) for compact Q
subproblem.statement: Let X be a metric space with its Borel σ-algebra, m ∈ ℕ, k > 0 real, Q ⊆ X compact and f : X → ℝᵐ continuous on Q. Then y ↦ 𝓗^k(Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}) (𝓗^k = (ω_k/2^k)μH[k] = Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal k) is a Borel measurable function ℝᵐ → [0,∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (m : ℕ) (k : ℝ) (Q : Set X) (f : X → Rn m), 0 < k → IsCompact Q → ContinuousOn f Q → Measurable (fun y ↦ Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal k (Q ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon leaves the measurability of y ↦ H^k(A ∩ f⁻¹y) in Theorem 1.9 as an exercise; this is the parent proof's completion, Part II, Step 2 (items 8-12), specialized to a compact set Q and a map f that is merely continuous on Q (the parent applies it with Q ⊆ A compact and f Lipschitz, hence continuous, on Q).

Conventions used below. (C1) All diameters are extended diameters ediam (Mathlib `Metric.ediam`, `ediam ∅ = 0`). (C2) For d ∈ ℝ, r ∈ (0,∞] and F ⊆ X put pre^d_r(F) := inf { Σ_{n∈ℕ} [t_n ≠ ∅](ediam t_n)^d : t : ℕ → Set X, F ⊆ ⋃_n t_n, ediam t_n ≤ r for all n }, where [t ≠ ∅]x := ⨆ (_ : t.Nonempty), x (that is, x if t ≠ ∅ and 0 if t = ∅). Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply` states exactly μH[d](F) = ⨆_{r>0} pre^d_r(F) for every F ⊆ X (no measurability needed). If 0 < r ≤ r' then pre^d_{r'}(F) ≤ pre^d_r(F), because every cover admissible at scale r is admissible at scale r'; in particular pre^d_r(F) ≤ μH[d](F) for every r > 0. (C3) For d ≥ 0 put c_d := ω_d/2^d, where ω_d = Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume d. Since 0 < ω_d < ∞ (`Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume_pos`, `Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume_ne_top`) and 0 < 2^d < ∞, we have 0 < c_d < ∞, and 𝓗^d(F) = c_d·μH[d](F) for every F ⊆ X (unfold `Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal d = (ω_d / 2^d) • μH[d]` and use `Measure.smul_apply`, `smul_eq_mul`). (C4) For δ ∈ (0,∞] and F ⊆ X define the finite open-cover content U_δ(F) := inf { Σ_{O∈𝒪} (ediam O)^k : 𝒪 a finite set of open subsets of X with ediam O < δ for all O ∈ 𝒪 and F ⊆ ⋃𝒪 } ∈ [0,∞] (inf ∅ = ∞). A convenient Lean encoding is ⨅ (𝒪 : Finset (Set X)) (_ : ∀ O ∈ 𝒪, IsOpen O ∧ ediam O < δ) (_ : F ⊆ ⋃ O ∈ 𝒪, O), ∑ O ∈ 𝒪, ediam O ^ k.

Proof.
1. (Reduction.) By (C3), 𝓗^k(Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = c_k·φ(y) with φ(y) := μH[k](Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}) and a constant c_k. So it suffices to prove that φ : ℝᵐ → [0,∞] is Borel measurable; then y ↦ c_k·φ(y) is Borel (`Measurable.const_mul`).
2. (Fibres are compact.) Q is a compact subset of the Hausdorff space X, hence closed. Since f is continuous on Q and {y} is closed in ℝᵐ, F_y := Q ∩ f⁻¹{y} is closed (`ContinuousOn.preimage_isClosed_of_isClosed`), and as a closed subset of the compact set Q it is compact (`IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset`).
3. (pre ≤ U for every set.) Let F ⊆ X and δ ∈ (0,∞]; then pre^k_δ(F) ≤ U_δ(F). Indeed, let 𝒪 = {O_1, ..., O_p} (pairwise distinct) be admissible for U_δ(F). The sequence t_n := O_{n+1} for n < p and t_n := ∅ for n ≥ p covers F and has ediam t_n ≤ δ for all n, so by (C2) pre^k_δ(F) ≤ Σ_n [t_n ≠ ∅](ediam t_n)^k ≤ Σ_{l=1}^p (ediam O_l)^k = Σ_{O∈𝒪}(ediam O)^k (the terms with n ≥ p vanish and [t ≠ ∅]x ≤ x). Taking the infimum over 𝒪 gives the claim.
4. (U ≤ pre for compact sets.) Let F ⊆ X be compact and δ ∈ (0,∞); then U_{2δ}(F) ≤ pre^k_δ(F). If pre^k_δ(F) = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise let ε > 0 and choose (definition of the infimum) sets C_n (n ∈ ℕ) with F ⊆ ⋃_n C_n, ediam C_n ≤ δ and Σ_n [C_n ≠ ∅](ediam C_n)^k ≤ pre^k_δ(F) + ε. For n with C_n = ∅ put O_n := ∅ (open, ediam ∅ = 0 < 2δ). For n with C_n ≠ ∅: ediam C_n ≤ δ < ∞, so (ediam C_n)^k < (ediam C_n)^k + ε·2^{-(n+1)}; since η ↦ (ediam C_n + 2η)^k is continuous on [0,∞) (`ENNReal.continuous_rpow_const`) and ediam C_n < 2δ, there is η_n ∈ ℝ≥0 with 0 < η_n and 2η_n < δ (i.e. η_n < δ/2) such that (ediam C_n + 2η_n)^k ≤ (ediam C_n)^k + ε·2^{-(n+1)}; put O_n := thickening (η_n : ℝ) C_n = {x : infEdist x C_n < η_n} (taking η_n in ℝ≥0 matches the form of `Metric.ediam_thickening_le (ε : ℝ≥0)`). Then O_n is open, C_n ⊆ O_n, and ediam O_n ≤ ediam C_n + 2η_n < δ + δ = 2δ (`Metric.ediam_thickening_le`). (Optional alternative, not needed for the argument: `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.exists_isOpen_superset_ediam_rpow_lt` in `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.HausdorffOpenCovers` (not imported by the frozen contract; add the import if used) yields, for ediam C_n < 2δ and (ediam C_n/2)^k < r, an open U ⊇ C_n with ediam U < 2δ and (ediam U/2)^k < r; with r := ((ediam C_n)^k + ε·2^{-(n+1)})/2^k this gives (ediam U)^k < (ediam C_n)^k + ε·2^{-(n+1)} after multiplying by 2^k and using (x/2)^k = x^k/2^k (`ENNReal.div_rpow_of_nonneg`).) Now F ⊆ ⋃_n C_n ⊆ ⋃_n O_n with all O_n open, so by compactness (`IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover`) there is a finite I ⊆ ℕ with F ⊆ ⋃_{n∈I} O_n. The finite set 𝒪 := {O_n : n ∈ I} is admissible for U_{2δ}(F); passing from the indexed family to the set 𝒪 only merges repeated sets, which drops nonnegative terms (`Finset.sum_image_le_of_nonneg`), and empty members contribute 0^k = 0 because k > 0. Hence U_{2δ}(F) ≤ Σ_{n∈I} (ediam O_n)^k ≤ Σ_{n∈I} ([C_n ≠ ∅](ediam C_n)^k + ε·2^{-(n+1)}) ≤ Σ_{n∈ℕ} [C_n ≠ ∅](ediam C_n)^k + ε ≤ pre^k_δ(F) + 2ε. Since ε > 0 is arbitrary, U_{2δ}(F) ≤ pre^k_δ(F).
5. (Identification on compact sets.) Put δ_n := 1/(n+1) ∈ (0,1] (as elements of ℝ≥0∞). For every compact F ⊆ X, μH[k](F) = ⨆_{n∈ℕ} U_{δ_n}(F). (≥) Step 4 with δ := δ_n/2 ∈ (0,∞) gives U_{δ_n}(F) = U_{2(δ_n/2)}(F) ≤ pre^k_{δ_n/2}(F) ≤ μH[k](F) by (C2). (≤) For r ∈ (0,∞] choose n with δ_n ≤ r (`ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt`); then pre^k_r(F) ≤ pre^k_{δ_n}(F) ≤ U_{δ_n}(F) by (C2) and step 3; taking the supremum over r > 0 in `hausdorffMeasure_apply` gives μH[k](F) ≤ ⨆_n U_{δ_n}(F).
6. (Upper semicontinuity.) Fix δ ∈ (0,∞] and put u_δ(y) := U_δ(F_y) for y ∈ ℝᵐ. Then u_δ is upper semicontinuous, i.e. for every y₀ ∈ ℝᵐ and every t > u_δ(y₀) there is a neighbourhood V of y₀ with u_δ(y) < t for all y ∈ V. Proof: by the definition of the infimum choose a finite set 𝒪 of open sets with ediam O < δ for O ∈ 𝒪, F_{y₀} ⊆ ⋃𝒪 and Σ_{O∈𝒪}(ediam O)^k < t, and put W := ⋃𝒪, an open set. The set Q ∖ W is compact (`IsCompact.diff`) and f is continuous on it, so f '' (Q ∖ W) is compact (`IsCompact.image_of_continuousOn`), hence closed in ℝᵐ. Moreover y₀ ∉ f '' (Q ∖ W), since every x ∈ Q with f x = y₀ lies in F_{y₀} ⊆ W. Hence V := ℝᵐ ∖ f '' (Q ∖ W) is an open neighbourhood of y₀. For y ∈ V and x ∈ F_y we must have x ∈ W (otherwise x ∈ Q ∖ W and y = f x ∈ f '' (Q ∖ W)), so F_y ⊆ W, 𝒪 is admissible for F_y, and u_δ(y) ≤ Σ_{O∈𝒪}(ediam O)^k < t. (If F_{y₀} = ∅, 𝒪 = ∅ and W = ∅ work.)
7. (Borel measurability of u_δ.) An upper semicontinuous function from ℝᵐ to [0,∞] is Borel measurable, since all its sublevel sets {u_δ < t} are open (`UpperSemicontinuous.measurable`).
8. (Conclusion.) By steps 2 and 5, φ(y) = μH[k](F_y) = ⨆_{n∈ℕ} u_{δ_n}(y) for every y ∈ ℝᵐ. A countable supremum of Borel functions is Borel (`Measurable.iSup`), so φ is Borel measurable, and by step 1 so is y ↦ 𝓗^k(Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to μH[k] since 𝓗^k = (ω_k/2^k)·μH[k]; each fibre F_y = Q ∩ f⁻¹{y} is compact.
Finite open-cover contents U_δ satisfy pre^k_δ(F) ≤ U_δ(F) for all F (pad finite covers with ∅).
For compact F, U_{2δ}(F) ≤ pre^k_δ(F): thicken near-optimal covers slightly and extract a finite subcover; hence μH[k](F) = ⨆_n U_{1/(n+1)}(F).
For fixed δ, y ↦ U_δ(Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}) is upper semicontinuous (compactness of f(Q ∖ ⋃𝒪)), hence Borel.
y ↦ μH[k](Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}) is a countable supremum of Borel functions, so y ↦ 𝓗^k(Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}) is Borel.

Compactness of f(Q ∖ W) proves upper semicontinuity; the countable supremum then gives Borel measurability. No global continuity, σ-compactness or finite fiber measure is assumed implicitly.

subproblem.title: Eilenberg covering estimate: Borel majorant of fibre Hausdorff measures
subproblem.statement: Let X be a metric space with its Borel σ-algebra (no σ-compactness, no measurability of E), m ∈ ℕ, k > 0 real, E ⊆ X with 𝓗^{m+k}(E) < ∞ (Simon-normalized 𝓗^s = (ω_s/2^s)μH[s] = Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal s, ω_s = Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume s), K ∈ ℝ≥0 and f : X → ℝᵐ K-Lipschitz on E. Then there is a Borel measurable G : ℝᵐ → [0,∞] with 𝓗^k(E ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ G(y) for every y ∈ ℝᵐ and ∫_{ℝᵐ} G dLᵐ ≤ (ω_m ω_k/ω_{m+k}) K^m 𝓗^{m+k}(E).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (m : ℕ) (k : ℝ) (E : Set X) (f : X → Rn m) (K : ℝ≥0), 0 < k → Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal (m + k) E < ⊤ → LipschitzOnWith K f E → ∃ G : Rn m → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable G ∧ (∀ y, Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal k (E ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}) ≤ G y) ∧ ∫⁻ y, G y ∂volume ≤ Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume (m : ℝ) * Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume k / Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume (m + k) * (K : ℝ≥0∞) ^ m * Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal (m + k) E
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. This is the covering half of the printed proof of Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 1.9 (pp. 45-46), in the completed form of the parent proof (Part II, Step 1, items 1-6). Printed text (cleaned transcription): 'For each i = 1, 2, ... pick closed subsets C_{i1}, C_{i2}, ... with diam C_{ij} < 1/i, A ⊆ ∪_j C_{ij} and (1) Σ_j ω_{m+k}(diam C_{ij}/2)^{m+k} ≤ H^{m+k}_{1/i}(A) + 1/i, and let g_i = Σ_j ω_k (diam C_{ij}/2)^k χ_{f(C_{ij})} ... (2) g_i(y) = Σ_{j : f⁻¹y ∩ C_{ij} ≠ ∅} ω_k(diam C_{ij}/2)^k ≥ H^k_{1/i}(A ∩ f⁻¹y), and hence ... ∫* H^k_{1/i}(A ∩ f⁻¹y) dLᵐ(y) ≤ ∫ g_i dLᵐ = Σ_j ω_k (diam C_{ij}/2)^k Lᵐ(f(C_{ij})) ≤ Σ_j ω_k ω_m (Lip f)^m (diam C_{ij}/2)^{m+k} ≤ (ω_mω_k/ω_{m+k})(Lip f)^m (H^{m+k}_{1/i}(A) + 1/i), where we used Lᵐ(f(C_{ij})) ≤ ω_m(diam f(C_{ij})/2)^m (isodiametric inequality 2.10) ≤ ω_m (Lip f)^m (diam C_{ij}/2)^m. Letting i → ∞ we conclude ...'. Documented corrections carried over from the parent proof: (a) f(C_{ij}) need not be Borel, so the indicator of the closed set closure f(C_{ij} ∩ E), which has the same diameter, is used instead; (b) instead of the upper integral ∫* of Remark 1.10, an explicit Borel majorant G := liminf_i g_i is built and Fatou's lemma is applied. The isodiametric inequality 2.10 is the kernel-checked SimonGMT theorem `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.simon_theorem_2_10 (n : ℕ) (A : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) : volume A ≤ realUnitBallVolume (n : ℝ) * (ediam A / 2) ^ (n : ℝ)` (valid for every n, including n = 0, and every set A); it lives in `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.EuclideanNormalization`, which must be imported (it is not imported by the frozen contract). No other erratum.

Conventions used below. (C1) All diameters are extended diameters ediam (Mathlib `Metric.ediam`, `ediam ∅ = 0`); `LipschitzOnWith K f E` means edist (f x) (f x') ≤ K·edist x x' for all x, x' ∈ E. (C2) For d ∈ ℝ, r ∈ (0,∞] and F ⊆ X put pre^d_r(F) := inf { Σ_{n∈ℕ} [t_n ≠ ∅](ediam t_n)^d : t : ℕ → Set X, F ⊆ ⋃_n t_n, ediam t_n ≤ r for all n }, where [t ≠ ∅]x := ⨆ (_ : t.Nonempty), x (that is, x if t ≠ ∅ and 0 if t = ∅). Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply` states exactly μH[d](F) = ⨆_{r>0} pre^d_r(F) for every F ⊆ X (no measurability needed). If 0 < r ≤ r' then pre^d_{r'}(F) ≤ pre^d_r(F), because every cover admissible at scale r is admissible at scale r'; in particular pre^d_r(F) ≤ μH[d](F) for every r > 0. (C3) For d ≥ 0 put c_d := ω_d/2^d, where ω_d = Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume d. Since 0 < ω_d < ∞ (`Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume_pos`, `Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume_ne_top`) and 0 < 2^d < ∞, we have 0 < c_d < ∞, and 𝓗^d(F) = c_d·μH[d](F) for every F ⊆ X (unfold `Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal d = (ω_d / 2^d) • μH[d]` and use `Measure.smul_apply`, `smul_eq_mul`). (C4) Fix the data of the statement and put s := m + k > 0, M := μH[s](E), c := ω_m ω_k/ω_s and a := ω_m ω_k K^m / 2^s. All of ω_m, ω_k, ω_s, K^m, 2^s are finite and ω_s, 2^s are nonzero, so c < ∞ and a < ∞.

Proof.
1. (Constant identity.) c·K^m·𝓗^s(E) = a·M. Indeed 𝓗^s(E) = (ω_s/2^s)·M by (C3), and (ω_mω_k/ω_s)·K^m·(ω_s/2^s) = ω_mω_kK^m/2^s = a because the factor ω_s ∈ (0,∞) cancels (ENNReal: `ENNReal.div_mul_cancel`/`ENNReal.mul_div_cancel` with ω_s ≠ 0, ω_s ≠ ⊤, plus commutativity and associativity).
2. (Finiteness.) 𝓗^s(E) = c_s·M < ∞ and c_s ≠ 0 give M < ∞. Hence pre^s_r(E) ≤ M < ∞ for every r > 0 by (C2).
3. (Near-optimal covers.) For i ∈ ℕ put δ_i := ε_i := 1/(i+1) ∈ (0,1] (as elements of ℝ≥0∞, (i+1)⁻¹). Because pre^s_{δ_i}(E) < ∞ and ε_i > 0, pre^s_{δ_i}(E) < pre^s_{δ_i}(E) + ε_i, so by the definition of the infimum (`iInf_lt_iff`) there is a sequence (C_{i,l})_{l∈ℕ} of subsets of X with E ⊆ ⋃_l C_{i,l}, ediam C_{i,l} ≤ δ_i for all l, and Σ_l [C_{i,l} ≠ ∅](ediam C_{i,l})^s ≤ pre^s_{δ_i}(E) + ε_i ≤ M + ε_i. Choose such a sequence for every i.
4. (Trimmed pieces.) Put D_{i,l} := C_{i,l} ∩ E and d_{i,l} := ediam D_{i,l}. Then d_{i,l} ≤ ediam C_{i,l} ≤ δ_i ≤ 1, so d_{i,l} < ∞. Because s > 0 we have d_{i,l}^s ≤ [C_{i,l} ≠ ∅](ediam C_{i,l})^s: if D_{i,l} = ∅ the left side is 0^s = 0; otherwise C_{i,l} ≠ ∅ and t ↦ t^s is monotone. Summing over l and using step 3: (★) Σ_l d_{i,l}^s ≤ M + ε_i.
5. (Image closures.) Put T_{i,l} := closure (f '' D_{i,l}) ⊆ ℝᵐ, a closed and therefore Borel set. For x, x' ∈ D_{i,l} ⊆ E, edist (f x) (f x') ≤ K·edist x x' ≤ K·d_{i,l}; hence ediam (f '' D_{i,l}) ≤ K·d_{i,l} (`Metric.ediam_le`), and since a closure has the same diameter (`Metric.ediam_closure`), ediam T_{i,l} ≤ K·d_{i,l}.
6. (Borel functions g_i.) Define g_i : ℝᵐ → [0,∞] by g_i(y) := Σ_{l∈ℕ} 1_{T_{i,l}}(y)·c_k·d_{i,l}^k (a tsum of `Set.indicator (T_{i,l}) (fun _ ↦ c_k * d_{i,l} ^ k)`). Each summand is a constant times the indicator of a closed set, hence Borel, and a countable sum of Borel [0,∞]-valued functions is Borel (`Measurable.ennreal_tsum`, deprecated but available; or `Measurable.tsum` from `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.Polish.Basic`). So every g_i is measurable.
7. (Pointwise bound at scale δ_i.) Fix y ∈ ℝᵐ and put F_y := E ∩ f⁻¹{y}. The sets t_l := D_{i,l} ∩ f⁻¹{y} (l ∈ ℕ) cover F_y (a point x ∈ F_y lies in E ⊆ ⋃_l C_{i,l}), satisfy ediam t_l ≤ d_{i,l} ≤ δ_i, and if t_l ≠ ∅ then y = f(x) for some x ∈ D_{i,l}, so y ∈ f '' D_{i,l} ⊆ T_{i,l}. Therefore [t_l ≠ ∅](ediam t_l)^k ≤ 1_{T_{i,l}}(y)·d_{i,l}^k for every l (k > 0, monotonicity of t ↦ t^k), and by (C2) pre^k_{δ_i}(F_y) ≤ Σ_l 1_{T_{i,l}}(y)·d_{i,l}^k. Multiplying by c_k (`ENNReal.tsum_mul_left`): c_k·pre^k_{δ_i}(F_y) ≤ g_i(y).
8. (Integral of g_i.) By the monotone convergence theorem for series (`lintegral_tsum`) and ∫⁻ 1_T·b dLᵐ = b·Lᵐ(T) for Borel T (`lintegral_indicator_const`), ∫⁻ g_i dLᵐ = Σ_l c_k·d_{i,l}^k·Lᵐ(T_{i,l}). By `simon_theorem_2_10` with n = m (rewrite the real exponent (m:ℝ) as the natural power m by `ENNReal.rpow_natCast`) and step 5, Lᵐ(T_{i,l}) ≤ ω_m·(ediam T_{i,l}/2)^m ≤ ω_m·(K·d_{i,l}/2)^m = ω_m·K^m·d_{i,l}^m/2^m (monotonicity of x ↦ (x/2)^m, `mul_pow`, `ENNReal.inv_pow`). Hence, writing d := d_{i,l} (finite), c_k·d^k·Lᵐ(T_{i,l}) ≤ (ω_k/2^k)·d^k·ω_m·K^m·d^m/2^m = (ω_mω_kK^m/2^{k+m})·d^{k+m} = a·d^s, using d^k·d^m = d^{k+m} (first rewrite the natural powers d^m and 2^m as real powers d^(m:ℝ), 2^(m:ℝ) with `ENNReal.rpow_natCast`; then `ENNReal.rpow_add_of_nonneg`, valid also for d = 0 since k ≥ 0 and (m:ℝ) ≥ 0), 2^k·2^(m:ℝ) = 2^{k+m} (`ENNReal.rpow_add`, as 2 ≠ 0, 2 ≠ ⊤) and k + m = m + k = s. (All factors are finite, so these identities may also be checked after passing to ℝ≥0.) Summing over l and using (★): (★★) ∫⁻ g_i dLᵐ ≤ a·Σ_l d_{i,l}^s ≤ a·(M + ε_i).
9. (The majorant.) Define G(y) := liminf_{i→∞} g_i(y) (`Filter.liminf (fun i ↦ g_i y) atTop`). G is Borel (`Measurable.liminf`).
10. (G dominates the fibre measures.) Fix y ∈ ℝᵐ and r ∈ (0,∞]. Choose i₀ with δ_{i₀} ≤ r (`ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt`). For every i ≥ i₀ we have δ_i ≤ δ_{i₀} ≤ r, so by (C2) and step 7, c_k·pre^k_r(F_y) ≤ c_k·pre^k_{δ_i}(F_y) ≤ g_i(y). Hence c_k·pre^k_r(F_y) ≤ ⨅_{i≥i₀} g_i(y) ≤ liminf_i g_i(y) = G(y). Taking the supremum over r > 0 and using (C3), (C2) and `ENNReal.mul_iSup`: 𝓗^k(E ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = c_k·⨆_{r>0} pre^k_r(F_y) = ⨆_{r>0} c_k·pre^k_r(F_y) ≤ G(y).
11. (Integral bound.) By Fatou's lemma (`lintegral_liminf_le`, all g_i measurable) and (★★), ∫⁻ G dLᵐ ≤ liminf_i ∫⁻ g_i dLᵐ ≤ liminf_i a·(M + ε_i). Since a < ∞, M < ∞ and ε_i = (i+1)⁻¹ → 0 (`ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero` composed with the shift i ↦ i + 1, e.g. via `tendsto_add_atTop_iff_nat 1`), a·(M + ε_i) → a·M (`ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul`, `Tendsto.const_add`), so this liminf equals a·M (`Tendsto.liminf_eq`), which equals c·K^m·𝓗^s(E) by step 1. Hence ∫⁻ G dLᵐ ≤ (ω_mω_k/ω_{m+k})·K^m·𝓗^{m+k}(E).
12. (Conclusion.) G is measurable (step 9), dominates y ↦ 𝓗^k(E ∩ f⁻¹{y}) everywhere (step 10) and satisfies the integral bound (step 11). The argument is uniform in K ≥ 0 and m ∈ ℕ (K = 0 and m = 0 included), because simon_theorem_2_10 holds in every dimension and every identity used above holds for these values. ∎
proof_key_steps: Constant identity c·K^m·𝓗^{m+k}(E) = (ω_mω_kK^m/2^{m+k})·μH[m+k](E) and finiteness of μH[m+k](E).
For δ_i = ε_i = 1/(i+1) choose near-optimal covers C_{i,l} of E from hausdorffMeasure_apply; trimmed diameters d_{i,l} = ediam(C_{i,l} ∩ E) satisfy Σ_l d_{i,l}^{m+k} ≤ μH[m+k](E) + ε_i.
Borel functions g_i = Σ_l c_k d_{i,l}^k 1_{closure f(C_{i,l} ∩ E)} satisfy c_k·pre^k_{δ_i}(E ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ g_i(y) for every y.
Isodiametric inequality (simon_theorem_2_10) and the Lipschitz diameter bound give ∫⁻ g_i ≤ (ω_mω_kK^m/2^{m+k})(μH[m+k](E) + ε_i).
G := liminf g_i is Borel, dominates 𝓗^k(E ∩ f⁻¹{y}) pointwise (sup over scales), and Fatou's lemma gives ∫⁻ G ≤ (ω_mω_k/ω_{m+k})K^m𝓗^{m+k}(E).
